name: New Zealand
genZNote: New Zealand was the first country in the world to give women the right to vote (1893) — a small, remote island nation that keeps quietly leading on progressive firsts, from suffrage to some of the earliest nuclear-free zone policies in the Pacific.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: An island nation in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, made up of two main islands (North and South Island) and numerous smaller islands.
Highly geologically active, sitting on the Pacific Ring of Fire, with significant volcanic and geothermal activity, alongside dramatic fjords and the Southern Alps mountain range.
One of the last major landmasses settled by humans, with Polynesian Māori voyagers arriving around 1250-1300 CE, followed by European settlement from the 17th-18th centuries.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: English, Māori, and New Zealand Sign Language are all official languages, reflecting a strong bicultural national identity between Māori and European (Pākehā) heritage.
The 1840 Treaty of Waitangi between the British Crown and Māori chiefs is considered the country's founding constitutional document, still central to ongoing rights and reconciliation discussions.
Rugby (particularly the All Blacks national team and their haka ritual) holds deep cultural and national significance.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A parliamentary constitutional monarchy; the British monarch is head of state (represented by a Governor-General), while an elected Prime Minister leads the government.
Was the first self-governing nation in the world to grant women the right to vote, in 1893, a landmark global first for suffrage.
Maintains a strong nuclear-free policy, refusing entry to nuclear-powered or nuclear-armed vessels since the mid-1980s, a distinctive and long-standing national security stance.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Home to Ernest Rutherford, the 'father of nuclear physics', a New Zealand-born Nobel laureate whose work laid foundations for atomic science.
A global leader in agricultural science and biotechnology, particularly in dairy farming and pastoral livestock management techniques.
Strong in geothermal energy technology, given its significant volcanic geology, generating a large share of domestic renewable electricity.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A member of the Commonwealth of Nations and maintains close security and trade ties with Australia through their long-standing 'Closer Economic Relations' agreement.
An active participant in Pacific regional diplomacy and a significant contributor to Pacific Islands development cooperation.
Known internationally for an independent foreign policy stance, including its distinctive nuclear-free zone policy.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and New Zealand maintain warm relations, with a growing Indian diaspora forming one of the country's largest and fastest-growing immigrant communities.
Growing trade and education ties, with New Zealand a popular destination for Indian international students.
Both countries collaborate on agricultural technology exchange, particularly dairy farming techniques relevant to India's dairy sector.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: An agriculture-driven economy, one of the world's largest dairy exporters, alongside significant meat, wool, and horticultural exports.
Tourism is a major economic pillar, drawing visitors to its dramatic natural landscapes, famously used as filming locations for major international productions.
A globally significant exporter of geothermal energy technology and expertise.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being the first country to grant women the right to vote (1893).
The All Blacks rugby team and the haka.
Dramatic natural landscapes, including fjords and geothermal features.
A long-standing nuclear-free zone policy.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: New Zealand Dollar (NZD).
An agriculture-driven economy, among the world's largest dairy and wool exporters, alongside a strong tourism sector.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Renowned for unique, isolated biodiversity, including the flightless kiwi bird and diverse endemic flora.
Extensive national park system; a global leader in ecological restoration and predator-control conservation programmes.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Settled by Polynesian Māori centuries before European contact.
The 1840 Treaty of Waitangi between the British Crown and Māori chiefs is the founding document of the modern nation.
Became fully independent within the Commonwealth in the 20th century.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1840 Treaty of Waitangi remains central to the country's constitutional and legal framework.
A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; in 1893 became the first self-governing country in the world to grant women the right to vote.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Home to Rocket Lab, a private company launching orbital rockets from New Zealand, making it one of the few countries with an active orbital launch site.
Strong biotechnology and agri-tech research sector.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Rugby is central to national identity, with the All Blacks among the most successful international teams in the sport.
Māori culture, including the haka and traditional carving, has strong global recognition.
Fiordland and other national parks are prominent UNESCO-recognised natural landscapes.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of the UN, the Commonwealth of Nations, and APEC.
Maintains a long-standing nuclear-free policy and close ties with Australia and Pacific Island nations.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: New Zealand is a Pacific island parliamentary constitutional monarchy, the first country to grant women's suffrage (1893), known for its bicultural Māori-European identity and nuclear-free policy.
keyFacts: Capital: Wellington (not Auckland). Currency: New Zealand Dollar.
Parliamentary constitutional monarchy; British monarch is head of state.
First self-governing nation to grant women the vote, in 1893.
Maintains a long-standing nuclear-free zone policy since the mid-1980s.
commonConfusion: New Zealand's capital is Wellington, not Auckland — Auckland is the largest city, but Wellington has been the capital since 1865.

highYieldFacts: New Zealand: parliamentary constitutional monarchy; capital Wellington; first nation to grant women's suffrage (1893).
Nuclear-free zone policy since the mid-1980s; 1840 Treaty of Waitangi is its founding constitutional document.
India-New Zealand: growing Indian diaspora and student population; agricultural (dairy) technology cooperation.
commonTraps: Assuming Auckland is New Zealand's capital — it is Wellington.
Confusing New Zealand's 1893 suffrage milestone with other countries' later women's voting rights dates.
mustRemember: New Zealand: first women's suffrage nation (1893), nuclear-free policy, Treaty of Waitangi foundation, growing India diaspora/education ties.
